AI/ML engineer focused on remote sensing and satellite-driven environmental solutions. I turn raw Earth observation data into tools that matter not just dashboards, but insights that drive real decisions.

Building a team for aiming to stand out globally, not just locally strong tech + powerful storytelling.

summary: AQUA SAR Eye is a working web prototype that shows how Lake Burullus, on Egypt's Nile Delta coast, changed between 2019 and 2026 using radar satellites. Radar works day and night and through clouds, so it can map water every year. Our featured layer is the new NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar (June to October 2026, provisional data). We classify it with its own machine-learning model and check it against Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical images. In the lake's 226 km2 permanent-water core, NISAR and Sentinel-1 agree within 1.4 km2 on open water. Sentinel-1 gives the 2019 to 2026 history: water and fish ponds fell from 288.5 to 270.5 km2 (-6.2%), mostly by 2023. The site has a map, a year slider, charts, tables and an AI chat assistant that only explains numbers computed by our analysis function. Radar shows what changed, not why, so we make no claims about causes. The tool gives researchers and decision-makers clear evidence to plan restoration and protect the fishing communities around the lake.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

AQUA SAR Eye gives decision-makers and researchers a ready analysis of Lake Burullus. The home page has a 3D Earth; the lake page has a map, a year slider (2019-2026), charts, tables and a chat assistant. The slider has two zones: Sentinel-1 archive years (blue) and the NISAR 2026 layer (gold).

HOW IT WORKS

1. NISAR (featured layer): five L-band GCOV scenes (path 129, frame 17; 23 Jun, 17 Jul, 22 Aug, 15 Sep, 21 Oct 2026, HH/HV, provisional) are combined into one composite. A separate Random Forest labels water, vegetation and land. Because HH brightness is sensitive to stems standing in water, we also measure bright non-water surface in the lake core (HH >= -14 dB) and validate it against Sentinel-2.

2. Sentinel-1 comparison and archive layer (2019-2026): one method, same season every year, fixed 496.6 km2 study area, processed in Google Earth Engine.

3. Labels and checks: Sentinel-2 gives training labels and a greenness reference; the JRC Global Surface Water map defines the 226.3 km2 permanent-water core and gives an independent check.

4. Backend (FastAPI on Vercel) serves map tiles and numbers. The chat assistant (an AI language model) only explains what our analysis function returns; a number guard blocks any number not in the analysis result.

MAIN RESULTS

- NISAR 2026 (provisional): 213.0 km2 of open water in the core (94.1%), within 1.4 km2 of Sentinel-1 (214.4 km2).

- NISAR sees 11.6 km2 of bright non-water surface in the core; 73% of it is green vegetation in Sentinel-2.

- Sentinel-1: water plus fish ponds fell from 288.5 km2 (2019) to 270.5 km2 (2026), -6.2%; most of the loss happened by 2023, then about flat.

- Accuracy: Sentinel-1 water vs non-water F1 about 0.98; four classes about 80%; NISAR model OA 0.82, water F1 0.95. About 99% of our water is also water in JRC.

- Trend is shown as a range (-0.85 to -4.22 km2 per year if the 2019-2026 trend continues), not a prediction; our backtest was off by about 10.5 km2.

HONEST LIMITS

NISAR data are provisional and cover one season. NISAR and Sentinel-1 are different sensors, so we never calculate a change between them. Validation uses Sentinel-2 and JRC, not field data. Radar shows what changed, not why, so we make no claim about causes. Not yet tested with real decision-makers.

IMPACT

Burullus gives about 19% of Egypt's fish production (published research). Clear evidence on what changed, where and by how much supports decisions to restore the lake and protect the fishing communities around it.

TOOLS

Google Earth Engine, Python, FastAPI, Vercel, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Three.js, MapLibre GL JS, Chart.js, ASF Data Search (NISAR). Code: https://github.com/yussef862/AQUA-SAR
